name: המרת שבר מדומה למספר מעורב (באנגלית)

functions.name: igcd2
functions.body: if q=0 then abs(p) else igcd2(q,mod(p,q))

questiontext:
Convert {{CT:0}} into a mixed fraction:

[[input:ans]]
[[validation:ans]]

Note, a mixed fraction might be written \(a\frac{b}{c}\) but you have to type: "a+b/c".
generalfeedback:
Outline: Divide the numerator by the denominator: the quotient is the whole part, and the remainder is the numerator of the fractional part (over the same denominator).
Step 1 — Division with remainder
Divide \({{CT:1}}\) by \({{CT:2}}\): \({{CT:2}}\) goes into \({{CT:1}}\) \({{CT:3}}\) times, since \({{CT:2}}\cdot {{CT:3}}={{CT:4}}\) and the remainder \({{CT:1}}-{{CT:4}}={{CT:5}}\) is smaller than \({{CT:2}}\). So

\[ {{CT:1}}={{CT:2}}\cdot {{CT:3}}+{{CT:5}} \]

Step 2 — Split the fraction
Substitute this into the numerator and split into two fractions:

\[ \frac{{{CT:1}}}{{{CT:2}}}=\frac{{{CT:2}}\cdot {{CT:3}}+{{CT:5}}}{{{CT:2}}}=\frac{{{CT:2}}\cdot {{CT:3}}}{{{CT:2}}}+\frac{{{CT:5}}}{{{CT:2}}}={{CT:3}}+\frac{{{CT:5}}}{{{CT:2}}} \]

The fractional part is smaller than 1 and in lowest terms, because \(\gcd({{CT:5}},{{CT:2}})={{CT:6}}\). As a mixed fraction this is \({{CT:3}}\frac{{{CT:5}}}{{{CT:2}}}\), which is typed as a sum:

\[ {{CT:7}} = {{CT:8}}. \]

on_true.feedback: Your answer is algebraically equivalent to the correct answer but you have not given your answer in its correct form or using fractions in lowest terms.
